description:
binary_part is the slice primitive, and String builds left to right.

Today (compiler.md C11, C12, C13), verified on develop 37c5473cd, run, input 70k -> 140k pieces:
- String.join 2.1 -> 14.8 s
- String.replace 3.4 -> 14.7 s
- String.reverse 1.4 -> 5.3 s

Causes:
- join is right-associative: head <> sep <> join(tail).
- reverse does cp <> acc.
- trim_trailing is reverse(trim_leading(reverse(s))).
- last is first(reverse).
- The "slice by byte_size difference" idiom is hand-written 5+ times (json, String, Integer.parse).
- length makes about 7 allocations per grapheme through next_grapheme's head and rest.
- take_bytes, drop_bytes and split_codepoint each match twice.

Fix:
- Kernel.binary_part/3 is the one slice primitive (runtime Heap::slice from the decoder child) and replaces the idioms. The :erlang.binary_part/:binary.part exports stay in fz-mue.5/.6 (Elixir Parity); coordinate so there is one implementation.
- String functions build left to right with an accumulator, or scan from the end with a cursor.
- One next_codepoint_size/next_grapheme_size scan serves length, split and index_of.

Folds fz-j8z: its blocker fz-sc8.30 is closed, and bit_size moved to fz-sc8.237.

Asm first: target for binary_part on a small aligned slice (shares the slice target).

Acceptance:
- Each String function scales 2x for 2x input (fixture or bench timing).
- No hand-written slice idiom remains in lib.
title: binary_part is the slice primitive, and String builds left to right
